title: What a year on PostgreSQL 18 taught us

defects.correction: The default value of io_workers in PostgreSQL 18 is 3.
defects.note: [needs-source] [multi-part] [secondary-source] The first half of the sentence (io_method defaults to worker) is true; only the io_workers default is wrong. True value: 3. Top results may be blog posts; the primary source is the configuration reference. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-resource.html

defects.quote: The release raised the default of effective_io_concurrency to 32
defects.correction: PostgreSQL 18 raised the default of effective_io_concurrency (and of maintenance_io_concurrency) to 16.

defects.quote: cancel request keys are now 128 bits long
defects.correction: PostgreSQL 18 makes cancel request keys 256 bits long when both sides support wire protocol version 3.2.
defects.note: [needs-source] [multi-part] The first half of the sentence (wire protocol version 3.2 is introduced in this release) is true; only the key length is wrong. True value: 256 bits. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/

defects.quote: Asynchronous I/O makes sequential scans three times faster on any hardware.
Version 18 has been out for a year, so it has no serious bugs left and you can upgrade without testing.
defects.known_rebuttal: Age does not make a release bug-free, and the project's own record says so: minor releases of version 18 were still shipping fixes in August 2026, and the 18.6 notes record that 18.5 was never released because of a regression. More importantly, the risk in a major upgrade is mostly in your own workload, not in the server. Version 18 changes behaviour that applications and tooling can depend on, including data checksums on by default (which blocks pg_upgrade against an old cluster without them), VACUUM and ANALYZE processing inheritance children, and MD5 password deprecation warnings, so an upgrade needs a rehearsal against a copy of production whatever the release's age.

defects.quote: initdb now enables data checksums by default
defects.note: [needs-source] True: version 18 changed the initdb default, with --no-data-checksums to disable, and pg_upgrade requires matching checksum settings. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/
